correctness.rationale: For all finite nonempty graphs, mu=sum(deg_i²)/(4m²) and edge insertion changes sum squares by exactly 2D+2, yielding the necessary-and-sufficient strict integer inequality in RESULT.md. For p=c/n+beta/n^(3/2), D is exactly Binomial(2n-4,p), edge and wedge counts have first-order limits, and the centered wedge-minus-c-edge statistic has the displayed exact orthogonal expansion, variance c²(1+c)n/2+o(n), Gaussian cumulants of higher order O(n), and mean c beta sqrt(n)/2+o(sqrt(n)). The fixed pair’s incident O_P(1) edges yield an O_P(1) effect on the global statistic, giving asymptotic independence. Off-lattice continuity and at-lattice exact inequality give the claimed Poisson-tail/Gaussian mixture; midpoint examples follow by Poisson arithmetic. The standalone checker reproduced 5,305 exhaustive edge-insertion tests and 3,288 exact weighted graph moment checks; simulation is supportive only. Assumptions c>0, beta fixed, n large, fixed pair absent, initial m>=1 are explicit; m=0 is an exponentially rare excluded convention.

value.rationale: In a cooperative simple voting game, adding a minimal winning pair is a natural operation representing a new decisive collaboration. The quadratic Deegan–Packel measure is already motivated as power concentration. The result quantifies the chance that this ostensibly expanding winning opportunity unexpectedly increases concentration, identifying a countably infinite series of discontinuities and the exact finite-size-scale Gaussian interpolation. This is an interpretable infinite-family structural probability theorem, not a small numerical example or a routine relabeling.
